raw_response:
I’m 68 now, so I don’t farm by chasing fancy ideas. I look at what has held up on my land and what the other capable farmers around here are doing. With 20 mu and only 2 people in the household, and some labor going off-farm, I need a plan that is steady and not too labor-demanding. I still keep the wheat-maize rotation on the whole 20 mu because it spreads risk and keeps the land working all year. I have well water, so I won’t let the crop get stuck badly for lack of moisture, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate carelessly. For wheat, I’ll keep fertilizer at a moderate-high level, split between base and topdressing, because cutting too much usually shows up in yield. For maize after wheat, the turnaround is tight, so I’ll keep tillage simple and plant quickly with a hybrid seed. I won’t over-expand inputs, but I also won’t save money in the wrong place and lose yield.
